A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RARO study. Their complete main texts and Appendices A-E, including equations, tables, figures and examples, support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and evaluation results on Countdown, DeepMath and Poetry Writing, including scaling experiments, component ablations and qualitative outputs.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds hyperparameter sensitivity results and measured training-step times.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the preliminary binary critic reward from p(expert)-p(policy), with signed outcome rewards, to p(expert), with 0/1 rewards. This is a limited reward reparameterization; final RARO's pairwise tie rewards, shared model, replay buffer and Algorithm 2 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Countdown, DeepMath and English Poetry Writing coverage. The added analyses concern existing tasks. HealthBench and EQ-Bench are newly discussed but are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark and test-time scaling comparisons retain Base, SFT, Rationalization, iterative DPO, RL-Logit and RLVR where applicable. DPO rounds and the two RL-Logit variants are retained; the RL-Logits spelling change does not introduce another comparator.

E3.justification: v4 adds coefficient sweeps and timing comparisons under matched hardware and rollout settings. Table 11 now describes RLVR selection as oracle best-of-N, whereas v1 describes the same tournament strategy as RARO. This revises the reported protocol without establishing a rerun; v4 retains conflicting same-strategy prose. Some qualitative-example model sizes also change from 1.5B to 7B.

E4.justification: v4 Section 6 adds sensitivity analyses of DeepMath tie rewards and poetry policy-loss weighting, while Appendix D.2 adds a compute-overhead analysis. Existing component ablations and training-failure analyses are retained, with the ablation table moved into the main text. Appendix E replaces the three policy case studies.

E5.justification: v1 reports standard deviations without explaining their estimation. v4 Section 4.3 specifies 100 bootstrap repeats on the test set. This newly documents uncertainty estimation; it does not establish additional independent training runs or seed replication.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark, scaling and component-ablation tables retain their numerical results. New Table 4 reports sensitivity outcomes, including DeepMath validation accuracies from 40.2 to 42.0. New Table 8 reports RARO/RLVR step times of 310/270 seconds on Countdown and 330/250 seconds on DeepMath. Policy examples are replaced, with different model sizes for DeepMath and poetry.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 revises the reward definition and policy-gradient derivation from p(expert)-p(policy) to p(expert), producing 0/1 critic rewards. v1's Proposition A.4 and its unbiased-estimator proof are removed. The closed-form optimal-policy and likelihood-gradient derivations in A.1-A.2 are retained.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain demonstration-only inverse-RL training, a relativistic reasoning critic, superiority over verifier-free baselines and favorable scaling across the same three tasks. v4 adds numerical margins to the abstract and introduction, but these already follow from v1's Tables 1-2.

C2.justification: v4 interprets the new sweeps as evidence against dependence on narrowly tuned coefficients and distinguishes moderate per-step overhead from poorer sample efficiency. It removes v1's broad inference that competing approaches struggle to generalize in open-ended domains. Existing limitations concerning creative-task instability, interpretability and scaling remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly clarifies that replay supplies critic input pairs, while policy rollouts remain fresh and stale critic outputs or policy log-probabilities are not reused. Appendix D.2 supplies measured step times. These improve documentation; the existing software stack, hardware allocations and core hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds discussion of Rubrics as Rewards, Beyond Verifiable Rewards and LLM-as-judge research, plus benchmark and software citations. It sharpens the distinction from prior IRL alignment work around joint adversarial training and reasoning. Tree of Thoughts, Buffer of Thoughts and DeepCoder citations disappear, while the central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The main narrative is substantially edited and reorganized: Preliminary becomes consolidated Related Work, latent-variable exposition moves into Method, and Experiments becomes separate Experimental Setup, Main Results and Ablation Studies sections. Method explanations are rewritten, an Impact Statement is added, and authorship/header text changes.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a two-column main-text layout, adds the RARO overview diagram, redraws and relocates plots, and reformats tables. The existing ablation table moves into the main text, sensitivity and timing tables are added, and the qualitative overview moves to the appendix with replacement policy examples.

improvement.justification: v4 provides useful additional sensitivity and runtime evidence, explains the previously unspecified uncertainty estimates, and clarifies replay-buffer operation. Its reorganized presentation makes the retained study easier to assess. These are incremental gains because the main experiments and findings are unchanged. The conflict between Table 11's oracle best-of-N description and the retained same-strategy TTS prose limits the improvement in protocol clarity.
